channel.title: Hlido — AI agent reviews
channel.description: Independent C2PA-verified reviews of AI agents. Every claim tested, scored on the Laddoo scale, signed with cryptographic provenance.

item.title: DevMate.AI — Laddoo 40/100
item.description: An AI-coding landing page with enterprise-grade claims and toy-grade evidence — big compliance promises, nothing on the public surface to back them.

item.title: ENZO — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: A self-hosted, bring-your-own-keys AI command center with a genuinely strong key-custody story — let down on the surface by rough edges and a pricing table that says nothing.

item.title: Foremerge — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: A deterministic, MCP-first coordination protocol for multi-agent coding — unusually honest about its own limits, and exactly the plumbing a fleet-of-agents future needs.

item.title: OtoDock — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: A self-hosted 'agentic company OS' on your own Claude/Codex subscription, with an unusually specific security model — ambitious in breadth, still asking to be taken on trust on most of it.

item.title: Radix — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A genuinely agent-native idea — a persistent visual workspace where a coding agent builds artifacts wired to your repo — behind a deliberately minimal, key-gated landing that gives Hlido almost nothing to verify.

item.title: rustunnel — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: An open-source, Rust-fast tunnel with a first-class MCP server — genuinely agent-drivable, priced to punish idle time, but the managed edge and reliability claims are asserted, not yet independently run.

item.title: Hello Aria — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: A chat-native personal productivity assistant that reaches you where you already are — WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, web and iOS — with real Google and Microsoft integrations, held back by marketing hype and thin trust transparency.

item.title: Driven — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A coherent, transparently-priced AI investment agent with broad market coverage — but its autonomous-execution headline is still aspirational and its trust claims lean on unverifiable social proof.

item.title: trace-mcp — Laddoo 77/100
item.description: A genuinely agent-native code-intelligence MCP server — open-source, local-first, broadly integrated — whose headline token-savings claims are asserted without a published, reproducible benchmark.

item.title: GoSQLX — Laddoo 75/100
item.description: A fast, well-presented multi-dialect SQL parsing SDK for Go with a genuinely agent-first MCP surface — but its headline performance and traction numbers are vendor-asserted and, in one case, don't reconcile.

item.title: kestra-io/mcp-server-python — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A credible, well-documented MCP server that exposes Kestra's workflow orchestration to agent clients like Claude, Cursor and VS Code — genuinely agent-first, though Hlido's capture landed on the parent blog rather than the repo, leaving repo-health signals unverified.

item.title: AceDataCloud MCP Nano Banana — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: A genuinely MCP-native image-generation server — four clean tools over Google's Nano Banana via AceDataCloud — but a thin, MIT-licensed wrapper whose reliability, traction, and image provenance all rest on an unverified third-party gateway.

item.title: Winx — Laddoo 78/100
item.description: A Rust MCP server that gives a coding agent a real PTY-backed shell with unusually careful safety engineering — impressively thorough for a project only days old.

item.title: medical-mcp — Laddoo 68/100
item.description: A broad, key-free MCP server over FDA, WHO, PubMed and RxNorm that installs in one click — but its privacy promise and its Google Scholar leg do not sit comfortably together.

item.title: Marzban — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: Marzban — open-source (AGPL-3.0) proxy-management panel: web UI, REST API, Telegram bot, multi-admin, multi-server scaling. Mature community project, docs navigated cleanly by our engine; capabilities self-described, nothing deployed. Infrastructure, not an AI agent. Tier-2 review; medium confidence.

item.title: Harden — Laddoo 85/100
item.description: Harden — local pre-execution monitor that checks coding-agent tool calls before they run (blocked/allowed/made-safe, on-device logs). Evidence-forward surface with live demo and baselined benchmarks; all figures self-reported. Tier-2 public-surface review; medium confidence.

item.title: Loqua — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: Loqua — AI voice dictation for Mac/Windows: global shortcut into any app, real-time cleanup, screenshot answers. Clear promise and accessible trial; headline numbers unverified and little exercisable public surface. Tier-2 review; medium confidence.

item.title: Concord AI — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A coordination layer for multi-agent coding — genuinely agent-native and unusually honest about its own evidence, but still waitlist-stage with the Cloud tier unshipped.

item.title: Mode — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: An AI design canvas that edits your real codebase — a sharp answer to throwaway-mockup drift, with transparent pricing but a login-gated product we couldn't run.

item.title: Naseem — Laddoo 79/100
item.description: A Mac-native coding agent with an unusually rigorous 'prove, don't assert' philosophy and transparent BYO-key pricing — genuinely differentiated, though young and untested by us behind the download.

item.title: Ouroboros — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: An open-source (MIT) spec-and-verify harness that sits around your coding agent — a strong idea with broad host support, still early and unverified by us at runtime.

item.title: Doop — Laddoo 77/100
item.description: An infinite design canvas that agents join over MCP as you, via OAuth — the most genuinely agent-native design surface we have reviewed, and free in beta with everything that implies.

item.title: Kombai — Laddoo 75/100
item.description: A design-and-code agent with a real thesis — make the design decisions deliberately, then write code that matches the repo it lands in — but nothing on the public surface an agent can drive.

item.title: Open Autonomy (Olas) — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: A mature, well-documented open-source framework for multi-agent services that settle on-chain — genuinely deep reference material, and a crypto premise you either need or you do not.

item.title: humanizer-ru — Laddoo 66/100
item.description: A single-purpose Russian-language checker for AI-paste traces that is unusually honest about its own state — versioned rules, a pinned commit, a published errata — but narrow, solo-maintained, and shipped alongside a rewriter that cuts the other way.

item.title: vlayer — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: Zero-knowledge infrastructure that lets Ethereum smart contracts verify real-world data — powerful primitives (Web/Email Proofs, Time Travel, Teleport), but reviewed here through docs the site itself flags as outdated.

item.title: Splitsense — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: An agentic CRO layer that connects to your analytics, scans the whole site, and ships conversion experiments automatically — a clear, well-told product story, but the proof on the page is a mockup, not customer evidence.

item.title: Topview — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: A broad, agent-native AI-video platform — many current models, a 'just tell your agent' creation flow, and transparent per-second pricing — held back mainly by breadth over demonstrated per-model quality.

item.title: Semiotic — Laddoo 75/100
item.description: A deep, mature React data-visualization library with an unusually broad chart catalog and a real accessibility discipline — a developer library, not an agent, and reviewed here through its documentation.

item.title: Reflexio — Laddoo 78/100
item.description: Agent infrastructure that turns real interactions — corrections, failures, wins — into reusable, visible, revocable 'learnings', with a genuinely well-explained mechanism and multiple clean integration paths.

item.title: Chronulus AI (MCP) — Laddoo 62/100
item.description: Forecasting-and-prediction agents exposed to Claude via an MCP server, with a genuinely useful cold-start (zero-history) angle — but 'predict anything' is a broad claim the public surface cannot substantiate, and traction is still early.

item.title: Dograh — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: Open-source, self-hostable voice-agent platform positioned squarely as the Vapi/Retell alternative — unusually broad provider matrix and a genuine air-gapped story, but the voice quality and privacy claims are untested on the public surface.

item.title: ReactUse — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: Mature, well-documented React hooks library (110+ hooks, TypeScript-first, SSR-safe) with a real MCP server so coding agents can query it — a solid developer utility whose 'agent' relevance is as a component, not an autonomous product.

item.title: Dingo — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: Comprehensive open-source data/model/application quality-evaluation toolkit that spans rule-based checks, LLM-as-a-judge and Agent-as-a-judge, including agent-trace evaluation — genuinely on-thesis for the agent era, reviewed here only at the surface.

item.title: Jupyter MCP Server — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: Well-documented open-source MCP server that lets an AI edit, document and execute Jupyter notebooks in real time — a clean, on-thesis agent-tooling bridge whose security and permission claims deserve verification before production use.

item.title: Zaturn — Laddoo 58/100
item.description: Open-source, local-first 'chat with your data' co-pilot that gives AI models SQL tools across many data sources, usable as an MCP server or a Jupyter-like studio — a promising, honest single-maintainer project that's early and asks you to bring your own LLM.

item.title: claude-mermaid — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: A two-tool MCP server that does one narrow job — live Mermaid previews inside Claude Code — and documents it better than most products ten times its size.

item.title: Proliferate — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: Open-source, self-hostable workspace for running coding agents in parallel — a review-first orchestration layer over Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Grok.

item.title: Excel MCP Server — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: MCP server that drives the real Microsoft Excel engine via its COM API — the honest, high-fidelity answer to Excel automation for agents, not another openpyxl file rewriter.

item.title: Srclight — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: Local-first code-indexing MCP server for AI agents — hybrid FTS5 + tree-sitter + embeddings in a single SQLite file, fully offline, 25 tools.

item.title: MCP-NixOS — Laddoo 78/100
item.description: MCP server that gives AI real, current NixOS / Home Manager / nix-darwin / flakes data so it stops hallucinating package and option names — narrow, well-built and context-frugal.

item.title: AnyFrame — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: A harness-agnostic platform for spinning up team agents inside Slack/Linear/GitHub — a clean concept and real SDK, but visibly pre-traction and crowded on differentiation.

item.title: Katalyst — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: A focused AI sales agent that keeps Salesforce current and preps reps for calls — named enterprise references and a real security posture, thin on programmatic openness.

item.title: Axel — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A native-Mac control room for dispatching coding agents — a thoughtful niche tool with a strong approval model, judged on a thin public surface.

item.title: ForceDream — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A genuinely agent-native execution runtime — discover, price, execute and cryptographically verify agent work over A2A/MCP — wrapped in oversized "sovereign OS" language and still very small.

item.title: Maritime — Laddoo 75/100
item.description: Agent-first hosting that gives every agent its own micro-VM at a flat $1/month — a genuinely differentiated infra bet, still early and self-benchmarked.

item.title: Framelink — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: Public-surface review of glips-figma-context-mcp.

item.title: Excel MCP Server — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: Public-surface review of haris-musa-excel-mcp-server.

item.title: EvalView — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: Public-surface review of hidai25-eval-view.

item.title: DroidMind — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: Public-surface review of hyperb1iss-droidmind.
